sentences.text: Acresuchus, meaning "Acre crocodile," is an extinct genus of medium-sized caiman found in western Brazil and Venezuela. The genus contains only one known species, Acresuchus pachytemporalis.
The holotype specimen UFAC-2507 is a nearly complete skull found in the Solimões Formation in Acre, while a skull fragment was found in the Urumaco Formation in Venezuela.
Acresuchus possesses large supratemporal fenestrae, which may be adaptations for large body size. These large openings may have aided in quicker prey capture and thermoregulation.

Acresuchus likely had a diet similar to the living black caiman due to shared features and size. Juvenile Acresuchus likely preyed on small invertebrates, while adults ate fish and small to medium-sized mammals.
Blunt teeth at the back of the skull suggest Acresuchus may have eaten hard-shelled animals.
Acresuchus is classified as a member of the subfamily Caimaninae and belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
The parent group of Acresuchus is the genus Jacarea, though this classification is noted alongside its placement in the subfamily Caimaninae.
Acresuchus lived during the Late Miocene epoch, specifically from the Tortonian to the Messinian stages, between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago.
